clinician.trajectory_summary: A 16-year-old male with no significant past medical history presented with a six-month history of epistaxis and nasal obstruction, initially treated with antibiotics for foul-smelling nasal discharge at another institution. He experienced progressive symptoms over three months with school withdrawal, 8 lb weight loss over one month, and mouth breathing due to obstruction. Physical examination revealed bilateral nasal polyposis and a centrally located soft palate mass that pressed the soft palate inferiorly and pointed the uvula anteriorly. MRI of the face and neck demonstrated a large, heterogeneously enhancing polypoid mass arising from the left nasal mucosa or left maxillary sinus extending into the nasopharynx and oropharynx, with abnormal signal enhancement in the left pterygopalatine fossa and left mastication space, and erosion of the left maxillary sinus medial wall. Two biopsies of the nasopharyngeal mass were obtained, showing granulation tissue and necrotic tissue with bacterial colonies, without malignancy. Surgical resection was subsequently performed. Final pathology of the surgical specimen confirmed the diagnosis of angiomatous inflammatory nasal polyp with no malignancy identified.
